title: Keeprite Furnace Code 2 Flash: Pressure Switch Stuck Closed
meaning: Two flashes mean the pressure switch stayed closed when the control expected it to open at startup.
diySteps: Turn off power.
Inspect the vent pipe and pressure tubing for blockages or standing water.
Clear the condensate trap if the hose runs through it.
whenToCallPro: If tubing is clear and the code returns, the pressure switch or inducer needs testing.
snippetAnswer: Keeprite furnace 2 flashes means the pressure switch is stuck closed at startup — venting or tubing is the usual cause. Check hoses and exhaust first; pro repairs run $175–$550.

title: Keeprite Furnace Code 3 Flash: Pressure Switch Stuck Open
meaning: Three flashes indicate the pressure switch never closed during the inducer cycle, blocking ignition.
diySteps: Inspect the vent termination outside for ice, debris, or bird nests.
Verify the small hose to the pressure switch is connected.
Clear clogged condensate from the trap on high-efficiency models.
whenToCallPro: If the inducer runs but the switch never closes, schedule inducer or switch service.
snippetAnswer: Keeprite furnace 3 flashes means the pressure switch never closed — inducer ran but vent proof failed. Blocked vents and condensate clogs are common; repairs run $175–$900.

title: Keeprite Furnace Code 4 Flash: Limit or Rollout Circuit Open
meaning: Four flashes signal the high-limit or flame rollout switch opened — overheating or combustion outside the burner box.
diySteps: Replace a dirty filter and open all supply vents.
Allow the furnace to cool for 30 minutes before resetting.
Do not bypass limit or rollout switches.
whenToCallPro: If four flashes return after restoring airflow, limit, rollout, or blower service is needed.
snippetAnswer: Keeprite furnace 4 flashes usually means limit or rollout opened — overheating from poor airflow is typical. Replace the filter first; pro limit or blower work runs $150–$600.

title: Keeprite Furnace Code 5 Flash: Abnormal Flame Signal
meaning: Five flashes mean the board detected flame when the gas valve should be off — an abnormal proving signal.
commonCauses: Gas valve leaking or slow to close
whenToCallPro: Unexpected flame signals require immediate professional inspection.
dangerNote: If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility before anything else.
snippetAnswer: Keeprite furnace 5 flashes means flame was sensed with no heat call — possible gas valve leak. Emergency: do not keep resetting; call a licensed tech; repairs run $350–$900.

title: Keeprite Furnace Code 6 Flash: Ignition Failure or Flame Lost
meaning: Six flashes indicate the burners failed to light or flame was lost while the furnace was running.
commonCauses: Rough ignition or low gas pressure
diySteps: Clean the flame sensor rod with fine steel wool.
Watch one ignition cycle for ignitor glow.
Reset power once after cleaning.
whenToCallPro: If flame still drops out, gas pressure and ignitor replacement need diagnosis.
snippetAnswer: Keeprite furnace 6 flashes means ignition failed or flame dropped out mid-cycle. Ignitor and flame sensor are the usual fixes; try a sensor clean first; repairs run $150–$450.

title: Keeprite Furnace Code 7 Flash: Limit Circuit Lockout
meaning: Seven flashes mean the limit or rollout circuit stayed open long enough to trigger a heating lockout.
diySteps: Replace the air filter and open all vents.
Allow a three-hour auto-reset or power-cycle once after cooling.
Monitor the next cycle closely.
whenToCallPro: Lockout after limit trips needs blower and limit switch inspection — do not keep forcing heat.
snippetAnswer: Keeprite furnace 7 flashes is a limit-circuit lockout after overheating trips. Fix airflow — new filter and open vents — then call a pro if it returns; repairs run $150–$600.

title: Keeprite Furnace Code 8 Flash: Gas Heating Lockout
meaning: Eight flashes indicate a gas heating lockout — the control will not retry until reset after a valve or ignition fault.
whenToCallPro: Gas heating lockouts require licensed diagnosis of the valve and control board.
dangerNote: If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility before anything else.
snippetAnswer: Keeprite furnace 8 flashes is a gas heating lockout — the board stopped all gas heat for safety. Do not bypass; call a licensed technician; typical repairs run $350–$900.

title: Keeprite Furnace Code 9 Flash: Two-Stage Pressure Switch Fault
meaning: Nine flashes mean the medium or high pressure switch (or its relay) did not close — or reopened — during an intermediate- or maximum-heat cycle on a two-stage or modulating furnace.
commonCauses: Failed medium or high pressure switch
Defective pressure switch relay on the control
diySteps: Check the vent and intake terminations outside for blockages.
Drain the condensate trap on high-efficiency models.
Note whether the code appears only when the furnace ramps to high heat.
whenToCallPro: Two-stage pressure faults need switch testing at high fire — schedule service if venting is clear.
snippetAnswer: Keeprite furnace 9 flashes means the medium or high pressure switch did not close during a high-heat cycle — a two-stage model fault. Check the vent outside first; pro repairs run $175–$550.

title: Keeprite Furnace Code 10 Flash: Reversed Line Polarity
meaning: Ten flashes indicate reversed 115V polarity or grounding problem at the furnace disconnect.
commonCauses: Hot and neutral swapped at disconnect
diySteps: Turn off power at the breaker.
Do not operate the furnace until wiring polarity is verified.
Confirm a proper ground bond to the cabinet.
whenToCallPro: Line voltage and grounding corrections require a qualified electrician or HVAC tech.
snippetAnswer: Keeprite furnace 10 flashes means reversed line polarity or bad ground at the furnace. Shut off power — this is an electrical safety issue; pro wiring correction runs $150–$350.
